units.blurb: Two texts studied through the lens of literary critical theory

topics.name: Elements of political and social protest writing
Two texts studied through the lens of literary critical theory

connections.why: Tragedy and comedy are the two alternative genre lenses in this unit; understanding either depends on the same idea that genre conventions shape meaning
Crime and protest writing are alternative genre studies that both read texts as members of a tradition with shared conventions
The generic reading skills from the tragedy unit carry directly into the crime-writing genre study
Comic subversion and protest both expose power and social order, inviting a genre-aware reading
Tragedy raises questions of fate, gender and power that critical theory (e.g. feminist, Marxist) reframes in the NEA
Comedy's treatment of class and gender is a natural target for the theoretical lenses applied in the coursework
Crime writing's concern with transgression and justice maps onto critical-theory readings of power and morality
Protest writing is explicitly political, lending itself to the Marxist and post-colonial frameworks of the theory unit
